Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — excited to get our BrightApps integration onto Redwood. Our main goals for the first 30 days are: keep 99th-percentile latency under 450ms for the interactive flow, and get per-token inference cost under $0.0009 for embeddings+chat mix. We expect a 3:1 mix (chat:embedding) during peak.

We have a short window before our marketing push on July 1, so would like a focused plan covering: recommended batching policy (target batch sizes / max latency trade-offs), KV/prefix caching strategy for our prompt templates, and safe quantization profiles to try without losing output fidelity. Also need an initial routing policy to favor low-cost model variants but fail over to high-quality variants for critical requests.

Can you propose a 2-week rollout plan (MVP tuning + verification) and who from your side should be on the implementation calls?

Hi Emma — great framing, thanks.

Quick answer up front: yes, we can meet the latency target with a combination of conservative batching, selective KV caching for your stable prompt prefixes, and a two-profile quantization rollout (Q4-safe and Q8-aggressive) gated by our output-regression checks. For routing, we'll use a weighted policy that prefers a smaller, quantized model for non-critical paths and a high-fidelity variant for verification/critical inference.

Proposed 2-week plan (high level):
- Day 0–2: kickoff + data access + mirror traffic rules (confirm sampling rates)
- Day 3–6: baseline collection (p95/p99, token distribution) + latency/cost simulation using your traffic trace
- Day 7–10: apply conservative batching & KV caching (measure) — deploy Q4 quant profile to a canary pool (5% traffic)
- Day 11–13: expand profiles (if no regression) to 25% and adjust batching thresholds; validate routing fallbacks and SLO alerts
- Day 14: rollout decision & handoff docs + mutual action plan signoff

Who should join from our side: Monica (systems tuning / batching), Marcus (quantization + perf regression harness), and Rishi (routing + capacity). I'll run the kickoff and coordinate procurement touches.

I'll attach a short checklist and our recommended quant profiles for initial testing. Can we do a 60-minute kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT?

Emma / team — adding a bit more technical meat so the implementation team can prep. Below are concrete starting knobs and guardrails we recommend for BrightApps' profile.

1) Batching policy
- Target: dynamic batching with latency cap of 300ms per request; max batch window 40ms, target batch size 8 for chat paths, 12 for embedding-only bulk calls.
- If client-reported max latency > 300ms, automatic switch to "small-batch" mode (batch size 2–3) for the next 1 minute.

2) KV (prefix) caching
- Cache stable prompt prefixes and the top 30 most-common user-level templates. TTL 12h for template-level artifacts; pinned KV entries for system prompts.
- Measure hit-rate expected uplift: 12–18% token reduction on average for templated flows.

3) Quantization profiles (safe rollout)
- Q4-safe: 4-bit quantization with per-channel smoothing + activation calibration — conservative selection for chat-critical routes.
- Q8-aggressive: 8-bit symmetric quant for embedding-heavy cheaper paths.
- Regression gating: automated BLEU/ROUGE-style pass on held-out prompts + manual QA for top-10 customer prompts. If delta_quality > 2% on measured metrics, rollback.

4) Routing policy (initial)
- Weighted routing: 70% -> Q8 model for non-critical inference (cheap path), 30% -> high-fidelity Q4 model. Critical flags from your side ("billing-check", "payment-confirm") always route to high-fidelity variant.

5) Observability & validation
- We'll run p95/p99 latency collectors and token-cost breakdown per route. Expect to see immediate token-cost reduction from caching and batching (benchmarks attached).

Attachments: quant-profiles-recommendation-v1.csv (CSV, 9 KB); latency-baseline-p99-20270614.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

If that looks good, Marcus and I can prepare the canary scripts and a short runbook for reversible deployments.

--
